thesis: Macro conditions are mixed but modestly restrictive for new equity risk. The Fed raised the policy range to 3.75%-4.00%, the 10-year real Treasury yield was 2.61% on Sep. 17, and inflation remains above target, all of which raise duration and discount-rate pressure. Against that, the NFCI remains looser than average and corporate credit spreads are tight, while private domestic demand is still resilient. Recommend risk_budget_multiplier 0.85: proceed, but pace entries rather than front-load risk.

evidence.claim: The FOMC raised the federal funds target range by 25 bp to 3.75%-4.00% on Sep. 16 and said inflation remained elevated.
The 10-year real Treasury yield was 2.61% on Sep. 17, up from 2.44% on Sep. 1, indicating a materially higher real discount-rate backdrop.
evidence.source: U.S. Treasury Daily Treasury Par Real Yield Curve Rates

evidence.claim: The Chicago Fed NFCI was -0.560 for the week ending Sep. 11; negative values indicate looser-than-average financial conditions.
evidence.source: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago / FRED NFCI

evidence.claim: Investment-grade corporate OAS was 0.78% and high-yield OAS 2.70% on Sep. 16, indicating no broad credit-market stress.
August CPI was 3.4% year over year and core CPI 2.4%, leaving headline inflation above the Fed's 2% target despite more moderate core inflation.
evidence.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI, August 2026

evidence.claim: Q2 real GDP grew 1.5% annualized, while real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.2%, showing softer headline growth but resilient private demand.
evidence.source: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis GDP second estimate, Q2 2026

counterevidence: Credit spreads and the NFCI remain benign, so monetary tightening has not translated into systemic stress.
The Fed characterized economic activity as expanding at a solid pace and domestic spending as resilient.
Core CPI at 2.4% year over year is materially closer to target than headline inflation, leaving room for inflation pressure to ease.
High-quality cash-generative companies with limited refinancing needs are less exposed to tighter funding conditions than the broader equity universe.
unknowns: Whether the Sep. 16 rate hike is followed by additional hikes in 2026.
How persistent the energy-driven component of headline inflation will be.
Whether long real yields remain above 2.5% or mean-revert after the policy repricing.
Whether currently tight credit spreads begin to widen if growth slows.
falsifiers: 10-year real yields fall materially while inflation continues to cool and credit spreads stay tight, which would justify moving the multiplier back toward 1.0 or above.
NFCI turns positive and IG/HY spreads widen sharply, which would require a substantially lower risk budget.
Growth reaccelerates without renewed inflation pressure, reducing the present duration-versus-growth tension.

key_kpis.name: 10-year real Treasury yield
key_kpis.threshold: Below ~2.25% would materially reduce duration pressure; sustained >2.75% would warrant more caution

key_kpis.name: NFCI / credit spreads
key_kpis.threshold: NFCI remaining negative and IG/HY spreads contained supports normal liquidity; abrupt widening signals stress

key_kpis.name: Inflation and policy path
key_kpis.threshold: Further disinflation without additional hikes would improve the risk budget

next_checks: Next FOMC communication and policy-rate path
September/October inflation releases and 10-year real-yield trend
NFCI and IG/HY OAS for signs of liquidity or credit deterioration
